verdict.rationale: Luma's legacy ReadMe-hosted Dream Machine reference has a runnable "Try It!" request panel against the live API, and each endpoint page carries an OpenAPI 3.1.0 definition. The current Luma Agents API docs, however, are a static reference with code samples and no runner, so the interactive experience exists only on the deprecated generation. Missing for 10: a runnable try-it on the current Agents API reference, a sandbox or free environment for test calls (the FAQ says there is none and the API is pay-as-you-go), a standalone downloadable spec, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can explore an interactive API reference with runnable examples

citations.quote: The legacy ReadMe-hosted reference runs the "Try It!" request panel against https://api.lumalabs.ai/dream-machine/v1.
the only runnable try-it is on the legacy-generation docs.
Luma's legacy Dream Machine API reference publishes per-endpoint OpenAPI 3.1.0 definitions in the markdown mirror of every reference page
